name: Lumentum

logo.source: commons.wikimedia.org (Lumentum logo dark 2015.svg; same artwork and size as the logo in lumentum.com header; en.wikipedia infobox has no logo)

description: Lumentum makes the lasers and optical parts that carry data: high-speed optical transceivers and the laser chips, photonic integrated circuits and photodiodes inside them for AI and cloud data centers, coherent and tunable components for metro and long-haul networks, plus industrial lasers (ultrafast and fiber lasers) and 3D-sensing laser emitters. It sells both components (67 percent of FY2026 revenue) and finished systems such as transceivers, optical circuit switches and industrial lasers (33 percent). Revenue rose 83 percent to $3.0B in fiscal 2026 and two customers were 27 and 15 percent. Net loss of $6.9B came almost entirely from a $7.76B non-cash loss on exchanging convertible notes for stock (the notes were converting at a value far above their principal: $7.76B of excess conversion value on about $1.1B of principal exchanged), not from operations, which earned $524.8M.

gics.note: Conventional GICS label as shown on Wikipedia's List of S&P 500 companies (columns GICS Sector and GICS Sub-Industry). That page does not show the industry group or industry, so those are null rather than filled from memory.

hq.note: Headquarters San Jose, California (FY2026 10-K); Delaware corporation

employees.note: About 13,757 full-time employees: 11,916 in manufacturing, 1,085 in R&D (FY2026 10-K)

businessLines.name: Components
businessLines.how: Parts sold per unit to system and transceiver makers, some of whom also compete with Lumentum; revenue follows data center and network build-outs and tight supply of laser chips.
businessLines.description: Semiconductor laser chips, laser sub-assemblies, line subsystems and wavelength-management systems: building blocks that customers integrate into their own systems (including the lasers inside other firms' transceivers).

businessLines.name: Systems
businessLines.how: Complete products sold per unit to network operators, cloud companies and industrial OEMs.
businessLines.description: Finished optical modules and transceivers (including coherent pluggables), optical circuit switches, and industrial lasers (short-pulse solid-state and kilowatt-class fiber).
